item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q008_v1_atp_synthase_bulge_classification","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, the V1 ATP synthase A-subunit bulge is family b.84.5.1 (SUNID 310616) within its own superfamily b.84.5 (SUNID 310577), rather than in b.84.1–b.84.4. All five superfamilies share fold b.84, whose annotation describes a sandwich of half-barrel-shaped beta sheets, but SCOPe explicitly does not infer homology at fold level. Thus the similar barrel-sandwich-hybrid architecture is insufficient evidence that the bulge descends from the proteins in the other b.84 superfamilies; resemblance there may be analogy or convergence. Conversely, superfamily placement does assert probable common ancestry within b.84.5, and the still narrower family b.84.5.1 groups the V1 bulge with the A1 ATP synthase A-subunit bulge as close homologs. This classification alone does not justify transferring detailed function, catalytic residues, interfaces, or organism-specific behavior from another b.84 superfamily. For modeling, b.84.1–b.84.4 members are structural analogs rather than homology templates; even a b.84.5.1 template requires compatible domain boundaries, sequence alignment, conformational/assembly context, and structure quality. The multiple V1 and A1 domain entries in the release also do not designate a universally representative structure, so representative selection needs those criteria rather than SCCS membership alone.
